references.text: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said. This is the first instance where Pharaoh's heart was hardened.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them. An earlier example of this same pattern of hardening.
Pharaoh hardened his own heart when he found relief from the plague of frogs. The same expression that Pharaoh hardened his own heart.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go. A continuation of the pattern of Pharaoh's hardened heart.
Pharaoh sinned again and hardened his heart. A parallel to Pharaoh's repeated hardening and refusal to let the people go free.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go. Part of the ongoing narrative about Pharaoh's hardening.
The Lord predicted that He would harden Pharaoh's heart so that he would not let the people go. God's prophecy concerning Pharaoh's hardening.
Paul quotes God's words to Pharaoh and explains that God hardens whom He wills. A theological reflection on Pharaoh's hardening in the New Testament.
Contrasts human resistance with divine sovereignty in the same event.
Links Pharaoh's action to the fulfillment of God's prophecy about his stubbornness.
A prophetic precursor (7:14) confirmed by the action (8:28).
Describes exactly the same dynamic: relief leads to immediate hardening.
Shows the same pattern: relief from judgment leads to active hardening.
Summarizes the whole picture by linking human resistance to divine sovereignty.
